summary.en-US: Browser control for coding agents, a command line for your tabs, and a userscript dev loop: build scripts on disk and push them straight into the browser. A Tampermonkey-compatible manager based on ScriptCat.

description.en-US:
LBcat is a browser extension plus local command line tools (bctl) that do three jobs in the browser you already use, with your logins. Install the tools from https://latentbyte.com/products/lbcat.

Browser control for coding agents
Claude Code, Codex, or any tool that can run shell commands uses bctl to open tabs, read pages, click, type, and take screenshots, inside one window you designate for agents.
- Scoped agent window: commands never fall back to your personal tabs, and a personal tab is only reachable when you grant that exact tab.
- Task sessions and tab leases let several agents share one browser without stepping on each other.
- When an agent needs you, it leaves a note on the tab and you get a desktop notification.

A command line for your tabs
List, focus, and close tabs across every window from the terminal, as plain text or JSON, for scripts, launchers, and tab switchers.

Userscripts from your editor to the browser
Write scripts in TypeScript or plain JavaScript and build them to .user.js. bctl installs each build in the browser as soon as the file is saved, with no copy and paste and no install dialog, and updates the installed copy in place on every push.

Why a ScriptCat fork
LBcat is built on ScriptCat and keeps its full Tampermonkey-compatible userscript manager. Agent control, the tab tools, and script pushes all need a native bridge between a local program and the extension, which upstream ScriptCat does not include, so Latent Byte added it and ships this signed build.

Local only: the tools talk to the extension over a local socket and Native Messaging. Nothing goes to a Latent Byte server. This is command targeting and task ownership, not a sandbox. Cookies and site state are shared with your profile, so only point agents you trust at it.

version.approval_notes: Source: the attached source zip (also https://github.com/latentbyte/lbcat). Build with Node 22+ and pnpm 10 (corepack enable): pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build:firefox && pnpm run pack. The Firefox package is dist/lbcat-<version>-firefox.zip. Each build embeds a fresh random key (SC_RANDOM_KEY in rspack.config.ts, inherited from ScriptCat, used to name the page-to-extension message channel), so a rebuild matches the upload except for that key and the few minified identifier names it shifts in content.js and inject.js. LBcat is a userscript manager: the eval and Function warnings come from running the scripts the user installs (sandbox, inject and content scripts), and the innerHTML warnings come from bundled libraries (Monaco editor, React, Arco Design). The optional local bctl CLI lives in the GitHub repo and is not part of the extension package.
